result.field: Information theory, interfaces and software architecture

whole.name: Pipes and filters over an immutable, content-addressed artifact store, with end-to-end integrity checks at the consumer (the dataflow or build-pipeline style)
whole.source: Shaw, M. and Garlan, D. (1996), Software Architecture: Perspectives on an Emerging Discipline, Prentice Hall (pipes and filters); Saltzer, J. H., Reed, D. P. and Clark, D. D. (1984), End-to-End Arguments in System Design, ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 2(4); Parnas, D. L. (1972), On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, CACM 15(12); content addressing as in Merkle, R. C., A Digital Signature Based on a Conventional Encryption Function, CRYPTO 87
whole.borrow: (1) Every intermediate is an immutable file recorded by its hash; nothing is regenerated, only re-read. (2) Every downstream record points straight to leaf records (card id, page hash plus quote offset), never to a summary of them, so pipeline depth does not compound loss. (3) A recognizer (schema validator script) sits at every pipe and rejects, never repairs, malformed input before any consumer that holds tools reads it. (4) The one integrity check that counts runs at the consumer end against the source bytes, by a script; checks at intermediate hops are only for early rejection. (5) Each filter's interface is versioned (a schema_version field) and fixed before the filter runs.

mappings.classical: Loss along a cascade of channels: the data processing inequality; lossy compression with an unspecified fidelity criterion (rate-distortion)
solutions: Data processing inequality [Shannon, C. E. (1948), A Mathematical Theory of Communication, Bell System Technical Journal; textbook statement in Cover, T. M. and Thomas, J. A. (1991), Elements of Information Theory, Wiley]
Rate-distortion: fix the distortion measure before compressing [Shannon, C. E. (1959), Coding Theorems for a Discrete Source with a Fidelity Criterion, IRE National Convention Record]
mappings.rule: Depth one from the leaves: every claim row in a review and in the synthesis carries card ids, and the card's typed condition fields are copied by a script, never retyped by a session. The coordinator's hand-over points at the watcher's status file (written by a script), never at a self-written summary. A defined distortion measure: a card is distorted when its source states a condition or caveat that changes the scope of the number and the card lacks it.
mappings.runner: The synthesis script, when it builds claims-table.json; the checker agent, for the distortion sample.
mappings.on_failure: A claim row whose card ids do not resolve, or whose copied conditions differ from the card's, is rejected back to its field as unbound and does not enter the synthesis. A field whose measured distortion D exceeds the owner's target fails its gate for the review.
mappings.formula: Retention end to end <= product over hops h of (1 - l_h). Measure per field: D = (checked cards with a scope-changing omitted condition) / (checked cards); binding loss b = (claim rows whose conditions differ from the cited card) / (claim rows). Target: b = 0 by construction (script copy), D below an owner threshold.
mappings.fails_here: Stages are not pure channels: a session can add invented content (noise that looks like signal), so loss is not only erasure. The distortion measure is not formal. The fix the field uses when you cannot code well is to break the chain: give each consumer a side channel to the source (a pointer), so the chain has depth one from every leaf.

mappings.classical: End-to-end integrity: checks at intermediate hops cannot assure correctness; only the endpoint, checking against the original, can. Plus error detection by redundancy (a check value bound to the data).
solutions: The end-to-end argument [Saltzer, J. H., Reed, D. P. and Clark, D. D. (1984), End-to-End Arguments in System Design, ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 2(4)]
Content addressing (hash of the bytes as the identity of the evidence) [Merkle, R. C., A Digital Signature Based on a Conventional Encryption Function, CRYPTO 87]
mappings.rule: The post-review check (P1) is the standard end-to-end check only once P21 is built: a Node script fetches the address itself (plain HTTP, HTML to text; PDF only if it can parse it), stores the bytes in the field folder under their sha256, normalises whitespace, case and Unicode, and looks for the card's quote. Redundancy that binds number to source: the card's number must also occur within a fixed window (for example 600 characters) of the quote's offset. The card records page_sha256 and quote_offset. Until the script exists, a card confirmed through the fetch tool is labelled confirmed-by-summary, not confirmed.
mappings.runner: The check script (Node), started by the child or by the coordinator's wave script; the checker agent only for the judgment part (does the citing sentence stay within the conditions).
mappings.on_failure: Status not-found or unfetchable: the card becomes unverified; every sentence citing it is re-labelled judgment and cannot carry a verdict. If the unverified share of cited cards exceeds the owner's threshold, the field's review fails its gate and is repaired once or dropped with a note.
mappings.formula: Per card: found = exists offset o with normalise(page)[o..o+len(q)] == normalise(q) (or edit distance <= 2 words); bound = number appears in normalise(page)[o-w, o+len(q)+w]. Field rates: f_found, f_bound, f_unfetchable.
mappings.fails_here: The endpoint check as currently run goes through the fetch tool, which returns a small model's summary: the check runs over the same lossy channel it is checking, which the end-to-end argument says buys nothing. Pages change, sit behind paywalls, or are PDFs a plain Node script may not parse. The field's answer when the end cannot be reached: the item is unverified, and no intermediate confirmation upgrades it.

mappings.classical: N-version programming and coincident (common-mode) failure: independently produced versions from one specification fail together
solutions: N-version programming [Avizienis, A. (1985), The N-Version Approach to Fault-Tolerant Software, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering SE-11(12)]

Experimental refutation of independence [Knight, J. C. and Leveson, N. G. (1986), An Experimental Evaluation of the Assumption of Independence in Multiversion Programming, IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering SE-12(1)]

Coincident-failure models and forced diversity [Eckhardt, D. E. and Lee, L. D. (1985), A Theoretical Basis for the Analysis of Multiversion Software Subject to Coincident Errors, IEEE TSE SE-11(12); Littlewood, B. and Miller, D. R. (1989), Conceptual Modeling of Coincident Failures in Multiversion Software, IEEE TSE 15(12)]
mappings.rule: Keep the current rule (agreement never raises a claim; disagreement marks it weak): it is the comparator use of N versions, the standard. Add what the field adds: (1) diversity is bought by method, not repetition: count a second opinion as independent only if it differs in model (F3) or in method (script quote check, contrary-evidence reader with its own query brief). (2) For F2 the field favours the second reviewer of the frozen pack plus diversity in model, over a second same-model research run: the run repeats the common-mode path (same model, same search tool) at the cost of a whole field. (3) Measure coincidence on seeded errors (D8-04) in the pilot.
mappings.runner: The coordinator's pilot scoring script, over the seeded-error results of two checkers or two reviewers.
mappings.on_failure: If the diversity factor shows the second same-model opinion catches almost nothing the first missed, the second same-model opinion is not bought in later waves; a different-model or script check takes its place, or none.
mappings.formula: p_A, p_B = miss rates on seeded errors; p_AB = joint miss rate. Diversity factor k = p_AB / (p_A * p_B): k = 1 independent, k -> 1/max(p) fully common-mode. Added detection by the second opinion = p_A - p_AB.
mappings.fails_here: Same model, same brief, same search tool: the strongest form of common mode. The field's response is forced diversity (different method, different input, different model) and measuring the coincidence rate instead of assuming it.

mappings.classical: Measuring the detection power of a checker: fault seeding and mutation analysis
solutions: Mutation analysis (seeded faults to measure a test's adequacy) [DeMillo, R. A., Lipton, R. J. and Sayward, F. G. (1978), Hints on Test Data Selection: Help for the Practicing Programmer, IEEE Computer 11(4)]
mappings.rule: Before the post-review check, a script copies the set of cited cards and citing sentences and plants m faults of four kinds: number changed, baseline swapped, condition dropped, sentence that claims beyond the card's conditions. The checker runs on the mixed set without knowing which are planted. For P13, the same idea certifies a reviewer: a separate calibration file of our work with known planted wrong assumptions, kept apart from the real review.
mappings.runner: The check script (plants, scores); the checker agent (checks blind).
mappings.on_failure: If detection q falls below the owner's threshold (for example 0.8), the field's confirmed labels are not accepted; the check is rerun with a different model or the field is marked unverified. Planted items are stripped by id before any file leaves the check.
mappings.formula: q = seeded faults detected / m. Estimated real faults left undetected ~ r * (1 - q) / q, with r = real faults found (seeding estimator; assumes equal detectability).
mappings.fails_here: A model may spot artificial-looking mutants; real faults of language models (plausible invented numbers, a dropped condition) must be mimicked. Seeded faults must never leak into files a review or synthesis reads.

mappings.classical: Input handling at a trust boundary: language-theoretic security (full recognition before processing), the critique of the robustness principle, and contracts at module interfaces
solutions: Language-theoretic security (LangSec) [Sassaman, L., Patterson, M. L., Bratus, S. and Shubina, A. (2011), The Halting Problems of Network Stack Insecurity, ;login: 36(6)]
Be strict in what you accept [Thomson, M. and Schinazi, D. (2023), RFC 9413, Maintaining Robust Protocols]
Design by Contract [Meyer, B. (1992), Applying 'Design by Contract', IEEE Computer 25(10)]
mappings.rule: Put the recogniser before the reader of the text: the child starts its readers through a workflow script; the script receives each reader's return, validates it against the card schema (closed set of keys, enumerated evidence label, numeric fields as numbers, quote of at most 15 words, each free-text field length-capped, no URL outside the address field), writes valid cards to cards.jsonl and rejected returns to a quarantine file the child does not open. The child reads only cards.jsonl. Reject, never repair. Every schema carries schema_version.
mappings.runner: The child's reader workflow script (Node).
mappings.on_failure: Rejected return goes to quarantine and is counted in the ledger; the sub-question is re-issued once to a fresh reader; a second rejection marks the sub-question not covered.
mappings.formula: Accept iff validate(card, schema_v) passes; rejection rate = rejected / returned per field.
mappings.fails_here: Free-text fields (conditions, limits, quote) are an unrestricted language inside a typed record: the schema recognises the envelope, not the content. And a helper's result returns into the child's window before any script sees it, so the recogniser runs after the consumer with tools has read the text, the reverse of LangSec's order.

mappings.classical: Precondition checking at a call site: using a component outside its contract (Design by Contract; type checking of a scope)
solutions: Design by Contract (precondition at the call site) [Meyer, B. (1992), Applying 'Design by Contract', IEEE Computer 25(10)]
mappings.rule: Treat a citation as a call: the card's typed conditions are its precondition (task kind, model family, repository size range, language, baseline kind, from enumerations); each approach id in the coordinator's approach list declares its scope in the same terms. A script flags every citing sentence whose approach scope lies outside the cited card's conditions; the checker judges only the flagged sentences and the prose residue.
mappings.runner: The check script (flags), then the checker agent (rules on flags).
mappings.on_failure: A sentence whose scope mismatch is upheld is re-labelled judgment and cannot carry a verdict; the out-of-conditions rate goes to the ledger.
mappings.formula: flag(sentence, card) = exists key k with scope[k] not within conditions[k]; mis-scope rate = upheld flags / citations.
mappings.fails_here: A card's conditions are mostly prose, so only part of 'used within its conditions' can be checked mechanically; the rest stays a judgment. The field's response is to make as much of the precondition typed as possible and leave the checker only the residue.

mappings.classical: Stage separation in a pipeline: a stateless filter over a persistent typed pipe versus fused stages with hidden state
solutions: Pipes and filters [Shaw, M. and Garlan, D. (1996), Software Architecture: Perspectives on an Emerging Discipline, Prentice Hall]
mappings.rule: Default the field's way: the review is a fresh filter over the frozen pack, must-read sections and our files, with one repair request back to research (a feedback channel, as in automatic repeat request). The pilot measures the hidden state instead of guessing: in the same-window review (written there for comparison), count factual sentences that cite nothing in the frozen pack. That count is exactly the information the pack failed to carry and that no check covered.
mappings.runner: The pilot's scoring script over both reviews.
mappings.on_failure: If the uncarried share is large, the pack's rate is too low: the fix is a pack rule (the researcher must add a card for anything a conclusion uses before freezing), not fusing the stages. If it is small, the fresh review is adopted.
mappings.formula: u = factual sentences in the same-window review citing no card in the frozen pack / factual sentences.
mappings.fails_here: The research session's window holds more than its pack (it read originals): fusing research and review uses that extra information but it is hidden state, unchecked and lost on any crash. By the data processing inequality the fused review can know more; the field's answer is not to fuse but to raise the pipe's rate until it carries what the review needs, with a feedback channel for what is missing.

mappings.classical: Module decomposition by information hiding; cohesion and coupling; a shared dependency factored into one owned module
solutions: Information hiding [Parnas, D. L. (1972), On the Criteria To Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 15(12)]
Cohesion and coupling [Stevens, W. P., Myers, G. J. and Constantine, L. L. (1974), Structured Design, IBM Systems Journal 13(2)]
mappings.rule: P11: the coordinator reading status files and verdicts only is information hiding and is the standard; keep it. P7: between waves the merge script builds a read-only source index (canonical id such as DOI or arXiv id -> card ids, page hash) from all finished fields; the next wave's readers get it as input and reuse a card instead of re-reading (re-checking its conditions only for their question). No writes during a wave, so no race; overlap within a wave stays accepted and counted. S: decide a split before research, never after, from measured coupling: after the pilot, cluster question ids by shared sources; a field is split only along a cut of low coupling.
mappings.runner: The wave merge script (index); the coordinator, reading its coupling table, for any split amendment.
mappings.on_failure: If the index is missing or stale, readers proceed without it (overlap only costs tokens, never correctness).
mappings.formula: Overlap rate = cards whose canonical id appears in more than one field / all cards. Coupling between question groups A and B = |sources(A) intersect sources(B)| / |sources(A) union sources(B)|.
mappings.fails_here: Field boundaries are drawn before anyone knows which sources are shared, so coupling is unknown until the pilot. A shared writable register breaks single ownership; the field's answer to a shared dependency is one owner and read-only users, not a shared write.

mappings.classical: Conway's law: a system's structure copies the communication structure of the organisation that builds it; what falls between groups is nobody's
solutions: Conway's law [Conway, M. E. (1968), How Do Committees Invent?, Datamation 14(4)]
mappings.rule: The coordinator's approved question list includes cross-field question ids (pairs of fields), each assigned to exactly one owning field and listed as input to the other. A coverage script counts cross-field ids answered by confirmed cards like any other id.
mappings.runner: The coordinator writes the ids (owner approves); the coverage script checks them.
mappings.on_failure: An uncovered cross-field id is listed as not covered in the synthesis, never silently absent.
mappings.formula: Cross-field coverage = cross-field ids with at least one confirmed card / cross-field ids.
mappings.fails_here: The tree forbids level-1 sessions from talking to each other, so the synthesis will have seven boxes and no edges: an interaction between two fields (for example caching with orchestration, small local models with graphs) is studied by no one. The field's response is to give the interfaces an owner.

mappings.classical: Evaluating retrieval when the set of relevant items is unknown: pooling, relative recall with known items, citation snowballing
solutions: Pooling for test collections [Spärck Jones, K. and van Rijsbergen, C. J. (1975), Report on the Need for and Provision of an 'Ideal' Information Retrieval Test Collection, British Library R&D report]
Pool bias measured [Zobel, J. (1998), How Reliable Are the Results of Large-Scale Information Retrieval Experiments?, SIGIR 1998]
Snowballing [Wohlin, C. (2014), Guidelines for Snowballing in Systematic Literature Studies and a Replication in Software Engineering, EASE 2014]
mappings.rule: Split each field's seed list at random by script: half goes in the readers' brief, half is held out. Coverage is estimated as relative recall on the held-out half. Diversify the pool: one reader per field searches by snowballing from the seed half rather than by keyword. The contrary-evidence reader stays.
mappings.runner: The coverage script (split before the wave, score after Stage A).
mappings.on_failure: Relative recall below the owner's threshold: the pack states its estimated coverage on its first page and the field gets one repair reader with a different strategy; it is not certified as complete.
mappings.formula: Relative recall r = |found intersect heldout| / |heldout|. Two readers with different strategies: Lincoln-Petersen N_hat = n1 * n2 / m (m = items both found); coverage = |union| / N_hat. Correlated readers make N_hat too low, so read it as an upper bound on coverage.
mappings.fails_here: All readers share one search tool and one model, so the pool is not diverse and its bias goes unmeasured. Seeds handed to readers cannot measure coverage: an item given in the brief is found by construction.

mappings.classical: Estimating the number of faults not yet found from overlapping independent inspections (capture-recapture)
solutions: Capture-recapture for inspections [Eick, S. G., Loader, C. R., Long, M. D., Votta, L. G. and Vander Wiel, S. (1992), Estimating Software Fault Content Before Coding, ICSE 1992]
Estimator for unequal catchability [Chao, A. (1987), Estimating the Population Size for Capture-Recapture Data with Unequal Catchability, Biometrics 43(4)]
mappings.rule: Use the expert lenses already being run (this task: each field lists risks the list lacks). A mapping step puts every finding onto a problem id, existing or new; a script counts, per id, how many lenses found it, and applies Chao's estimator.
mappings.runner: The coordinator's mapping agent (assigns ids), then a scoring script.
mappings.on_failure: If the estimated unseen count exceeds a small threshold (for example 2), one more lens from a field not yet asked is run before the list is called complete.
mappings.formula: Chao: N_hat = S_obs + f1^2 / (2 * f2), with f1 = problems found by exactly one lens, f2 = by exactly two. Estimated unseen = N_hat - S_obs.
mappings.fails_here: Same-model lenses are positively correlated, which biases the estimate low; lenses from different fields are heterogeneous, which the Chao estimator tolerates. Treat the result as a lower bound on what is missing.

missing.title: The seams between fields are nobody's job
missing.classical: Conway's law (Conway 1968)
missing.mechanism: Cross-field question ids with one owner each, counted by the coverage script (D8-09).

missing.title: The schema guarantees what it carries, and so hides what it dropped
missing.classical: Lowest-common-denominator data format in pipes and filters (Shaw and Garlan 1996); silent loss outside the fidelity criterion
missing.mechanism: A counted overflow field on cards and reviews; the checker's distortion sample (D8-01) reports caveats lost for want of a field; the schema gains a field when one kind of loss repeats.

missing.title: The same original counted twice through secondary sources

do_not: Do not chain summaries: no stage may summarise a summary; every record points to the leaf (card, page bytes).
Do not take agreement between instances of one model as independent confirmation, and do not vote on facts.
Do not verify through the channel you are verifying (the fetch tool's summary is not the source).
Do not repair malformed hand-overs; reject them (be strict in what you accept at a trust boundary).
Do not let a session that holds tools read untrusted text before a script has recognised it against the schema.
Do not hand all seed papers to the readers if you want to know the search's coverage; hold half out.
Do not add an untyped free-text 'notes' field to a typed interface; it becomes the channel everything leaks through.
Do not decompose after the fact: decide boundaries before work, from measured coupling, never by cutting a finished expertise.
Do not share one writable file between writers to save duplicate work; one owner, read-only users, merged between waves.
Do not count a check as a guarantee until its detection rate on seeded faults is known.

sources_with_a_problem.source: Shannon 1948; Cover & Thomas 1991
sources_with_a_problem.correction: Attribute the DPI to Cover & Thomas (a textbook statement); present the product bound as a separate strong-DPI result or a heuristic.
sources_with_a_problem.note: Both works exist (from recall). The data processing inequality I(X;Z)<=I(X;Y) for a Markov chain is stated in Cover & Thomas, not in Shannon 1948 as such. The plain inequality does not give 'retention is at most the product of per-hop retentions'; that needs strong-data-processing contraction coefficients and is not a consequence of the DPI alone.
